inspections.anchor: [18] Seonghyuk Im, Ruonan Li, and Hong Liu, Sidorenko’s conjecture for subdivisions and theta
inspections.note: Publication data of Im, Li and Liu: Combin. Probab. Comput. 35 (2026), no. 2, 269–279.

problem.text: Transporting Sidorenko and forcing properties through graph-substitution operators by an adjoint identity.

claims.text: Theorem 2.4: every gadget substitution L_{F,a,b,c} has a right adjoint. Proposition 2.2 and Corollary 2.5: such operators preserve the Sidorenko property under an edge-count or edgelessness condition. Proposition 1.1: balanced blow-ups of Sidorenko graphs are forcing, and blow-ups preserve forcing families. Propositions 1.2 and 1.3: Cartesian and strong products with a bipartite graph preserve forcing families when that graph is added. Proposition 1.4: subdivisions preserve forcing families. Proposition 1.5: G box F box Q_n is forcing for Sidorenko G and F with F dominated by Q_{n+2}.

assumptions.text: Graphons on standard probability spaces with vertex-colored densities; the forcing property in its graphon form.

methods.text: Adjoint identities for substitution operators with vertex-colored right adjoints, zero sets of density equations, and Lebesgue-point arguments for the equality cases.

evidence.text: Complete proofs for the graph results; the hypergraph extension of Section 5 is described as expected, not proved.

limitations.text: The operators preserve properties that the input already has; none produces a Sidorenko graph from a graph whose status is unknown. The hypergraph extension is not developed. The authors leave open which adjoints have the substitution form.

relevance.text: No result of this paper decides the girth-six statement or its declared neighbours; its subdivision results transport properties that the base graph already has. It confirms the state of the subdivision question as of 21 September 2026, two days before the reported counterexample: the 1-subdivision of every Sidorenko graph is Sidorenko (CKLL, Theorem 1.3(ii)), the 1-subdivisions of complete graphs and of 1-skeleta of regular polytopes are weakly norming (Conlon and Lee), and the 1-subdivision of a KNRS graph is Sidorenko; no result settles the 1-subdivision of an arbitrary graph. Proposition 1.4 concerns the forcing neighbour: if a family is forcing, so is its k-subdivision. It also gives the journal publication of Im, Li and Liu (Combin. Probab. Comput. 35 (2026), 269-279) and cites Baek, Conlon and Lee on the extremal number of incidence graphs (arXiv:2501.00521).
